sentences.en: ANNIE: OK, Jack
sentences.zh: ANNIE: 好的，杰克。

sentences.en: Before we plan our presentation about refrigeration, let's discuss what we've discovered so far
sentences.zh: 在我们规划关于制冷技术的演示文稿之前，先来讨论一下截至目前我们已有的发现。

sentences.en: JACK: Fine, Annie
sentences.zh: JACK: 好的，安妮。

sentences.en: Though I have to admit I haven't done much research yet
sentences.zh: 不过我得承认，我目前还没做多少研究。

sentences.en: ANNIE: Nor me
sentences.zh: ANNIE: 我也是。

sentences.en: But I found an interesting article about icehouses
sentences.zh: 但我发现了一篇关于冰窖的有趣文章。

sentences.en: I'd seen some 18th- and 19th-century ones here in the UK, so I knew they were often built a in a shady area or underground, close to lakes that might freeze in the winter
sentences.zh: 我在英国这里见过一些18世纪和19世纪的冰窖，因此我知道它们通常建在阴凉处或地下，靠近冬季可能结冰的湖泊。

sentences.en: Then blocks of ice could be cut and stored in the icehouse
sentences.zh: 这样就可以切割冰块并储存在冰窖中。

sentences.en: But I didn't realise that insulating. 021 the blocks with straw or sawdust meant they didn't melt for months
sentences.zh: 但我之前并不知道，用稻草或锯末对冰块进行隔热处理，能使它们数月不融化。

sentences.en: The ancient Romans had refrigeration, too
sentences.zh: 古罗马人也拥有制冷技术。

sentences.en: JACK: I didn't know that
sentences.zh: JACK: 我以前不知道这一点。

sentences.en: ANNIE: Yes, pits were dug in the ground, and snow was imported from the mountains - even though they were at quite a distance
sentences.zh: ANNIE: 是的，他们在地上挖坑，并从山区运来积雪——即使那些山区距离相当遥远。

sentences.en: The snow was stored in the pits
sentences.zh: 积雪被储存在这些坑中。

sentences.en: Ice formed at the bottom of it
sentences.zh: 坑底会结成冰。

sentences.en: Both the ice and the snow were then sold
sentences.zh: 之后，冰和雪都会被出售。

sentences.en: The ice cost more than the snow and my guess is that only the wealthy members of society could afford it
sentences.zh: 冰的价格比雪更高，我猜测只有社会上的富裕阶层才买得起。

sentences.en: JACK: wouldn't be surprised
sentences.zh: JACK: 我一点也不奇怪。

sentences.en: I also came across an article about modern domestic fridges
sentences.zh: 我还读到一篇关于现代家用冰箱的文章。

sentences.en: Several different technologies are used, but they were too complex for me to understand
sentences.zh: 其中采用了多种不同技术，但对我来说过于复杂，难以理解。

sentences.en: ANNIE: You have to wonder what happens when people get rid of old ones
sentences.zh: ANNIE: 你有没有想过，人们淘汰旧冰箱时会发生什么？

sentences.en: JACK: You mean because the gases in them are harmful for the environment?
sentences.zh: JACK: 你是说因为冰箱里的气体对环境有害？

sentences.en: ANNIE: Exactly
sentences.zh: ANNIE: 没错。

sentences.en: At least there are now plenty of organisations that will recycle most of the components safely, but of course some people just dump old fridges in the countryside
sentences.zh: 至少如今已有大量机构能安全回收冰箱的大部分零部件，但当然仍有人直接把旧冰箱丢弃在乡间。

sentences.en: JACK: It's hard to see how they can be stopped unfortunately
sentences.zh: JACK: 很遗憾，很难阻止这种行为。

sentences.en: In the UK we get rid of three million a year altogether!
sentences.zh: 仅在英国，我们每年总共淘汰三百万台冰箱！

sentences.en: ANNIE: That sounds a lot, especially because fridges hardly ever break down
sentences.zh: ANNIE: 这个数字听起来很大，尤其是因为冰箱几乎从不损坏。

sentences.en: JACK: That's right
sentences.zh: JACK: 没错。

sentences.en: In this country we keep domestic fridges for 11 years on average, and a lot last for 20 or more
sentences.zh: 在我们国家，家用冰箱平均使用年限为11年，很多甚至能用20年或更久。

sentences.en: So if you divide the cost by the number of years you can use a fridge, they're not expensive, compared with some household appliances
sentences.zh: 因此，若将购买成本按可使用年数来分摊，与其他一些家用电器相比，冰箱其实并不昂贵。

sentences.en: ANNIE: True
sentences.zh: ANNIE: 的确如此。

sentences.en: I suppose manufacturers encourage people to spend more by making them different colours and designs
sentences.zh: 我想制造商是通过推出不同颜色和设计来鼓励人们增加消费。

sentences.en: I'm sure when my parents bought their first fridge they had hardly any choice!
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定，我父母当年买第一台冰箱时，几乎没什么选择余地！

sentences.en: JACK: Yes, there's been quite a change. a
sentences.zh: JACK: 是的，变化确实相当大。

sentences.en: JACK: Right, let's make a list of topics to cover in our presentation, and decide who's going to do more research on them
sentences.zh: JACK: 好了，我们先列出演示文稿需涵盖的主题，并确定谁负责对哪些主题做进一步研究。

sentences.en: Then later, we can get together and plan the next step
sentences.zh: 之后，我们再聚在一起规划下一步工作。

sentences.en: ANNIE: OK
sentences.zh: ANNIE: 好的。

sentences.en: How about starting with how useful refrigeration is, and the range of goods that are refrigerated nowadays?
sentences.zh: 我们先从制冷技术的实用性入手如何？以及如今需要冷藏的各类商品范围？

sentences.en: Because of course it's not just food and drinks
sentences.zh: 毕竟，需要冷藏的当然不只是食品和饮料。

sentences.en: JACK: No, I suppose flowers and medicines are refrigerated, too
sentences.zh: JACK: 对，我想鲜花和药品也需要冷藏。

sentences.en: ANNIE: And computers
sentences.zh: ANNIE: 还有计算机。

sentences.en: I could do that, unless you particularly want iO
sentences.zh: 我可以做这个，除非你特别想做iO部分。

sentences.en: JACK
sentences.zh: JACK。

sentences.en: No, that's fine by me
sentences.zh: 不，我完全没问题。

sentences.en: What about the effects of refrigeration on people's health?
sentences.zh: 关于冷藏对人们健康的影响呢？

sentences.en: After all, some of the chemicals used in the 19th century were pretty harmful, but there have been lots of benefits too, like always having access to fresh food
sentences.zh: 毕竟，19世纪所用的一些化学物质危害性相当大，但同时也带来了诸多益处，比如人们可以随时获得新鲜食品。

sentences.en: Do you fancy dealing with that?
sentences.zh: 你愿意负责这一部分吗？

sentences.en: ANNIE: I'm not terribly keen, to be honest
sentences.zh: ANNIE: 说实话，我对这个不太感兴趣。

sentences.en: JACK: Nor me
sentences.zh: JACK: 我也不感兴趣。

sentences.en: My mind just goes blank when read anything about chemicals
sentences.zh: 一读到任何有关化学物质的内容，我的脑子就一片空白。

sentences.en: ANNIE: Oh, all right then
sentences.zh: ANNIE: 哦，那好吧。

sentences.en: I'll do you a favour
sentences.zh: 我来帮你个忙。

sentences.en: But you owe me, Jack
sentences.zh: 但你欠我一个人情，杰克。

sentences.en: OK
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: What about the effects on food producers, like farmers in poorer in countries being able to export their produce to developed countries?
sentences.zh: 关于冷藏对食品生产者的影响呢？比如较贫穷国家的农民得以向发达国家出口农产品。

sentences.en: Something for you, maybe?
sentences.zh: 这部分交给你，怎么样？

sentences.en: JACK
sentences.zh: JACK。

sentences.en: I don't mind
sentences.zh: 我不介意。

sentences.en: It should be quite interesting
sentences.zh: 这应该会相当有趣。

sentences.en: ANNIE: I think we should also look at how refrigeration has helped whole cities like Las Vegas, which couldn't exist without refrigeration because it's in the middle of a desert
sentences.zh: ANNIE: 我觉得我们还应考察冷藏如何帮助整座城市的发展，例如拉斯维加斯——若没有冷藏技术，这座城市根本无法存在，因为它地处沙漠腹地。

sentences.en: JACK: Right
sentences.zh: JACK: 没错。

sentences.en: I had a quick look at an economics book in the library that's got a chapter about this sort of thing
sentences.zh: 我在图书馆快速翻阅了一本经济学书籍，其中有一章专门讨论这类问题。

sentences.en: I could give you the title, if you want to do this section
sentences.zh: 如果你要负责这一部分，我可以把书名告诉你。

sentences.en: ANNIE: Not particularly, to be honest
sentences.zh: ANNIE: 说实话，我并不特别想做。

sentences.en: I find economics books pretty heavy going, as a rule
sentences.zh: 一般来说，我觉得经济学类书籍读起来相当晦涩难懂。

sentences.en: JACK: OK, leave it to me. then
sentences.zh: JACK: 好吧，那就交给我来处理。

sentences.en: ANNIE: Thanks
sentences.zh: ANNIE: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Then there's transport, and the difference that refrigerated trucks have made
sentences.zh: 然后还有运输领域，以及冷藏卡车所带来的变化。

sentences.en: I wouldn't mind having a go at that
sentences.zh: 我倒不介意尝试一下这部分。

sentences.en: JACK: Don't forget trains, too
sentences.zh: JACK: 别忘了还有火车。

sentences.en: I read something about milk and butter being transported in refrigerated railroad cars in the USA, right back in the 1840s
sentences.zh: 我读到过一些资料，提到早在19世纪40年代，美国就已使用冷藏铁路车厢运输牛奶和黄油。

sentences.en: ANNIE: hadn't thought of trains
sentences.zh: ANNIE: 我之前还真没想到火车。

sentences.en: Thanks
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: JACK: Shall we have a separate section on domestic fridges?
sentences.zh: JACK: 我们是否该为家用冰箱单独设立一个章节？

sentences.en: After all, they're something everyone's familiar with
sentences.zh: 毕竟，这是人人都熟悉的东西。

sentences.en: ANNIE: What about splitting it into two?
sentences.zh: ANNIE: 不如把它分成两部分呢？

sentences.en: You could investigate 19th- and 20th- century fridges, and I'll concentrate on what's available these days, and how manufacturers differentiate their products from those of their competitors
sentences.zh: 你可以研究19世纪和20世纪的冰箱，而我则专注于当今市面上的产品，以及制造商如何使其产品区别于竞争对手。

sentences.en: JACK: OK, that'd suit me
sentences.zh: JACK: 好的，这样安排我很满意。
